The must-sees

  • Austrian Parliament

    Civic building · 1883

    Theophil Hansen designed it in a classical style to recall the birthplace of democracy, and it was finished in 1883. Austria’s National Council and Federal Council meet inside.

    Look for: Athena holds a small winged Victory in her hand; the reclining figures below stand for the rivers Danube, Inn, Elbe and Vltava.

  • Belvedere

    Palace · 1723

    The Upper and Lower Belvedere were built in the early 1700s. The Austrian Gallery holds the largest Klimt collection, including The Kiss.

    Look for: From the terrace of the Upper Belvedere, the gardens lead your eye down to the spire of St Stephen’s Cathedral.

  • Hofburg

    Palace · 1279

    The imperial residence grew from a medieval castle into a complex of wings. The Spanish Riding School and the imperial apartments are inside.

    Look for: The red, black and gold Swiss Gate from the 1550s leads into the oldest courtyard, the Swiss Court.

  • Karlskirche

    Church · 1737

    Vowed during a plague in 1713 and dedicated to St Charles Borromeo. The oval dome and the spiral reliefs on the columns are the set piece.

    Look for: In the pond in front sits Henry Moore’s bronze Hill Arches.

  • Kunsthistorisches Museum

    Museum · 1891

    Opened in 1891 to house the imperial collections. Bruegel, Vermeer, and the Kunstkammer of curiosities are the reasons to stay.

    Look for: Above the arches of the main staircase are paintings by the young Gustav Klimt, his brother Ernst and Franz Matsch.

  • Natural History Museum

    Museum · 1889

    It opened in 1889 to house the imperial natural collections. Its best-known object is the Venus of Willendorf, around 30,000 years old.

    Look for: Between the two museums, Maria Theresa sits on a high bronze throne, surrounded by her generals and advisers.

  • Schönbrunn

    Palace · 1780

    Rebuilt in the 18th century for Maria Theresa, it has 1,441 rooms. The Gloriette on the hill looks back over the yellow facade.

  • St. Stephen’s Cathedral

    Church · 1433

    A church has stood here since the 12th century. The south tower, the Steffl, was finished in 1433 and is still the city’s landmark.

    Look for: Left of the main door, two iron bars set in the wall are old Viennese measures of length, used to check cloth sold in the market.

  • Vienna State Opera

    Culture · 1869

    The original opened in 1869 and was mocked at first. It burned in 1945 and reopened in 1955.

    Look for: In the loggia above the Ring, frescoes by Moritz von Schwind show scenes from Mozart’s The Magic Flute.

How it works

  1. Open Wizzy in Vienna and tap Start walk, or pick a ready-made walk.
  2. Put your phone in your pocket. Wizzy runs in the background, even with the screen locked.
  3. When you pass a place, you get a ping. Open it for the story, or keep walking.

Every place you see gets stamped in your Vienna passport. Your location stays on your phone. No ads, no tracking.
